title: Evaluation formula for the canonical internal compact-support adjunction
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring, let $f:X\to S$ be compactifiable [def-asd-compactifiable] between Noetherian schemes, and work in the ordinary unbounded etale derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], with derived tensor [def-kun-derived-tensor] and internal Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Let $M\in D(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and $K,Q\in D(S_{\mathrm{et}},A)$. Write $\alpha_{f,M,K}:Rf_*R\mathcal Hom_A(M,f^\times K)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\mathcal Hom_A(Rf_!M,K)$ for the canonical internal adjunction [prop-asd-internal-adjunction], with $Rf_!$ the ordinary etale compact direct image [def-amb-etale-compact-support] and $f^\times$ its right adjoint [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint], and $\varepsilon_{f,K}:Rf_!f^\times K\to K$ for the exceptional counit. For a map $h:Q\to Rf_*R\mathcal Hom_A(M,f^\times K)$ let $p:f^*Q\otimes_A^L M\to f^\times K$ be its transpose under ordinary inverse-image and tensor--Hom adjunction. The tensor--Hom transpose of $\alpha_{f,M,K}\circ h$ is precisely
$$Q\otimes_A^L Rf_!M\xrightarrow{\Pi_{f,Q,M}}Rf_!(f^*Q\otimes_A^L M)\xrightarrow{Rf_!(p)}Rf_!f^\times K\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_{f,K}}K.$$
Here $\Pi_{f,Q,M}$ is the canonical compact-support projection isomorphism: for a compactification $f=rj$, first apply the proper counit-defined projection map of [lem-amb-proper-coproducts-projection], then the extension-by-zero tensor identification [lem-pur-etale-open-derived-tensor] $r^*Q\otimes_A^L j_!M\cong j_!(f^*Q\otimes_A^L M)$. This normalizes the displayed map on the ambient ordinary etale categories; it makes no constructibility assertion.

source.place: Proof, last paragraph: evaluation and exceptional counit underlying the internal adjunction; see also prop-asd-internal-adjunction proof, displayed Hom bijections

proof.text:
Write $H=R\mathcal Hom_A(M,f^\times K)$ and $U=Rf_*H$. We first spell out the ordinary inverse-image transpose on the unbounded categories. By [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], $f^*=f^{-1}$ is exact on constant-$A$ modules and is left adjoint to $f_*$. Choose a complex $T$ for a test object $B$ and a K-injective complex $I$ for $H$ by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. Degreewise adjunction gives
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{K(S)}(T,f_*I)=\operatorname{Hom}_{K(X)}(f^*T,I):$$
it carries a chain homotopy $a-b=ds+sd$ to the same equation, by naturality of the sheaf adjunction. For acyclic $T$, $f^*T$ is acyclic, so this equality says that $f_*I$ is K-injective. The two applications of [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] therefore give
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{D(S)}(B,U)=\operatorname{Hom}_{K(S)}(T,f_*I)=\operatorname{Hom}_{D(X)}(f^*B,H).$$
Here $f_*I$ computes $Rf_*H$ by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived]: the functor $Q_Sf_*$ on homotopy categories is exact because additive $f_*$ respects the finite-sum matrices defining shifts and cones. These are natural bijections, and their inverse-image counit is denoted $e:f^*U\to H$.

source.place: Tag 07A6, lemma-adjoint; explicit exact-inverse-image specialization using derived.tex Tag 070I, lemma-K-injective, and Tag 070K, lemma-enough-K-injectives-implies

proof.text:
For either small etale ringed site, put $H_A(C,D)=R\mathcal Hom_A(C,D)$. Apply $H^0$ of derived global sections to the natural isomorphism $H_A(B,H_A(C,D))\cong H_A(B\otimes_A^L C,D)$ of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction]. Applying [lem-pur-rhom-global-sections] to its two sides gives the natural bijection
$$c_{B,C,D}:\operatorname{Hom}(B,H_A(C,D))\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}(B\otimes_A^LC,D).$$
Its evaluation is $\operatorname{ev}_{C,D}=c_{H_A(C,D),C,D}(1)$. Naturality in $B$ gives $c(a)=\operatorname{ev}_{C,D}\circ(a\otimes1_C)$, by substituting $a:B\to H_A(C,D)$ into the naturality square for the identity. Thus this is exactly the tensor--Hom transpose convention of the statement.

Choose a compactification $f=rj$ by [def-asd-compactifiable]. Its middle scheme is Noetherian: $r$ is of finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism], hence locally of finite type and quasi-compact by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]; [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] gives local Noetherianity. A finite affine cover of $S$, together with finite affine covers of its inverse images under $r$, gives quasi-compactness and a finite cover of the middle scheme by Noetherian affines. Apply [lem-amb-proper-coproducts-projection] to $j_!M$. Using $Rf_!=Rr_*j_!$ of [def-amb-etale-compact-support], compose its map with [lem-pur-etale-open-derived-tensor] to obtain
$$\Pi_{B,M}:B\otimes_A^LRf_!M\xrightarrow{\sim}Rr_*(r^*B\otimes_A^Lj_!M)\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_!(f^*B\otimes_A^LM).$$
In the second arrow interchange tensor factors, apply the cited open comparison, and interchange them back. This uses exactly the sign symmetries specified in the proper projection statement, not an independently chosen isomorphism. The identification $j^*r^*=f^*$ is composition of the ordinary inverse images. Both arrows are natural in $B,M$, and neither citation requires boundedness or constructibility. This is the projection map normalized in the item.

source.place: Proof, third displayed bijection: proper projection formula on a compactification, preceded by extension by zero

proof.text:
The Noetherian compactification of step 3 satisfies [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint], so $F=Rf_!$ is left adjoint to $G=f^\times$. Apply the inverse-Hom formula of [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection] with $P=f^*B\otimes_A^LM$. It sends a map $p_B:P\to f^\times K$ to exactly
$$\varepsilon_{f,K}\circ Rf_!(p_B):Rf_!(f^*B\otimes_A^LM)\longrightarrow K.$$
This fixes the direction and the counit of the exceptional transposition. It uses the ordinary unbounded exceptional adjunction, with $A$ finite as assumed, and imposes no invertibility condition on $|A|$.

source.place: Tag 0037, definition-adjoint and following unit/counit formulas; blueprint prop-asd-internal-adjunction.proof.md, second displayed bijection

proof.text:
Set $V=R\mathcal Hom_A(Rf_!M,K)$. For every test object $B$ compose the bijections of steps 1, 2 and 4, precomposition with $\Pi_{B,M}$ of step 3, and the inverse of the bijection of step 2 on $S$. This gives a bijection $\Phi_B:\operatorname{Hom}_S(B,U)\to\operatorname{Hom}_S(B,V)$. Explicitly, if $a:B\to U$ and $p_B=c(e\circ f^*a)$, then
$$\Phi_B(a)=c_{B,Rf_!M,K}^{-1}\bigl(\varepsilon_{f,K}\circ Rf_!(p_B)\circ\Pi_{B,M}\bigr).$$
Each constituent is natural in $B$: the two adjunctions and $c$ are natural Hom bijections, and $\Pi$ was shown natural in step 3. Their composite and its inverse are consequently natural in $B$. This is the full chain of Hom bijections in the blueprint, now with every arrow specified.

source.place: Proof, full displayed chain of natural Hom bijections

proof.text: Define $\theta=\Phi_U(1_U):U\to V$ and $\psi=\Phi_V^{-1}(1_V):V\to U$. Naturality gives $\Phi_B(a)=\theta\circ a$ and $\Phi_B^{-1}(b)=\psi\circ b$. Taking $B=U,a=1_U$ and then $B=V,b=1_V$ in the inverse identities yields $\psi\theta=1_U$ and $\theta\psi=1_V$. Hence $\theta$ is the isomorphism represented by the displayed Hom bijections. This construction identifies $\theta$ with the canonical $\alpha_{f,M,K}$ named in [prop-asd-internal-adjunction]: it is precisely the canonical representative of the chain in that source, rather than an arbitrary isomorphism between $U$ and $V$. No evaluation formula is taken from the proof of that node as a black box; the preceding steps constructed the representing map.

source.place: Proof, Yoneda sentence, expanded by evaluating the natural bijections and their inverses at identities

proof.text:
Apply step 5 to $B=Q,a=h$. The map $p_Q=c(e\circ f^*h)$ is the $p$ in the item, by steps 1 and 2. Step 6 gives $\Phi_Q(h)=\alpha_{f,M,K}\circ h$. Apply $c_{Q,Rf_!M,K}$ to the equality of step 5; the consecutive $c,c^{-1}$ cancel. The resulting map is
$$\varepsilon_{f,K}\circ Rf_!(p)\circ\Pi_{Q,M},$$
with the projection map of step 3 and the exceptional counit of step 4. This proves the asserted equality of morphisms for every $h$, on the ambient ordinary etale categories.

source.place: Proof, final evaluation/counit sentence; specializes the explicit Hom-bijection calculation to the given h
